title: Chest Pain and Shortness of Breath Post-Hysterectomy

patient.name: Jen Carter
patient.persona: A 52-year-old female bank administrator who speaks clearly and provides detailed responses, volunteering relevant information such as recent surgery and lifestyle habits without prompting.
patient.openingLine: I’ve had chest pain for just over a week and it’s causing trouble breathing.

presentingProblem: chest pain with associated shortness of breath

facts.text: I’ve had this pain in my chest for just over a week now and it’s caused me to have trouble breathing.
facts.quote: I so I've just had this pain in my chest for just over a week now and it's caused me to have trouble breathing.

facts.text: The chest pain is sharp and constant, but worsens when I take a deep breath.
facts.quote: Ahh it it is, but it's definitely worse that um, it's the breathing that's been bothering me a lot more. When I take a deep breath that the pain is a lot worse.

facts.text: Each episode of pain lasts about 15 to 20 minutes before easing off.
facts.quote: Um I would say, uh. Around 15-20 minutes. It's it goes away over overtime.

facts.text: I get short of breath when I exert myself, like walking a few blocks, but it improves when I rest.
facts.quote: Uh no if I if I take a break or sit down to rest then I can usually catch my breath. But if even if I'm doing a little bit of exertion like walking a few a few blocks or something like that I'm finding it, I'm I'm short of breath.

facts.text: My shortness of breath reaches up to 7 or 8 out of 10 during exertion.
facts.quote: I would say when I'm exerting myself, it could get up to like a 7 or 8.

facts.text: Before this, I used to run a few days a week, but now I can only walk about 100 meters before needing to rest.
facts.quote: I I would say maybe 100 meters. But before I was able to run uh like I was running a few days per week so. So this is not like me.

facts.text: I’ve had a dry cough for about a week, which started around the same time as the chest pain.
facts.quote: Yeah, it's um. I still have a cough.

facts.text: I had a hysterectomy a few weeks ago due to heavy bleeding from fibroids.
facts.quote: No, like I've been um previously healthy, but I I guess I did have a hysterectomy a few weeks ago. I know it was, I I didn't bring it up before 'cause it's just a day procedure, but I was definitely spending a lot more time um relaxing at home after that, a few weeks ago.

facts.text: I smoke about half a pack of cigarettes per day and have smoked since my teenage years.
facts.quote: Um I I smoke, I may be about half a pack of cigarettes per day. I've smoked ever since I was a teenager.

facts.text: I occasionally have a glass of wine on weekends but otherwise do not drink alcohol.
facts.quote: Uh may be a glass of wine on the weekends, but other than that no.

facts.text: My mother had a heart attack at age 56.
facts.quote: Yeah, it's just my mom had a heart attack when she was 56.

facts.text: I sometimes feel like my heart is racing, especially when I move around more.
facts.quote: Uh, actually I did feel like that a little bit. Especially when I was moving a little bit more, I felt like my heart was racing.

facts.text: My left leg feels a little sore, though I’m not sure if there’s swelling.
facts.quote: Um yeah my left, my left leg's actually a little bit sore.

facts.text: I am concerned this might be something serious like a blood clot, given my recent surgery and symptoms.
facts.quote: I I had a cough about a week ago so I thought it might be a chest infection, but I'm not feverish, so I'm not sure.

redFlags.label: Asks about recent surgery combined with unexplained leg pain or swelling
redFlags.exampleQuestion: Have you noticed any pain, swelling, or redness in your legs since your hysterectomy?
